title: Justify the Text

concept.title: Greedy line packing, then spread the spaces
body: Put as many words as possible on a line: keep adding the next word while the words and **one space between each pair** still fit into the width `W`. Then the extra room is spread over the gaps. With `spaces = W - (total letters)` and `slots = count - 1` gaps, every gap gets `spaces // slots` spaces, and the first `spaces % slots` gaps get one more.

body.code:
base, extra = divmod(spaces, slots)
gaps = [base + 1 if k < extra else base for k in range(slots)]

body: Two special cases are not stretched: a line with a single word (it has no gap) and the last line of the text. They use single spaces between words and the rest of the width is empty space at the end. To make the result checkable, this problem asks you to print, for each line, the layout as numbers instead of the text itself.

statement: A text of `n` words must be arranged in lines of exactly `W` characters. Fill each line greedily with as many words as fit, with at least one space between neighbouring words. Then distribute the remaining spaces: every gap between words gets the same number of spaces; if they cannot be divided evenly, the left gaps get one extra space each. A line with only one word, and the last line, are not stretched: words in them are separated by exactly one space and the remaining spaces come after the last word.
Instead of the text, print the layout of every line: the number of words `k`, then the `k - 1` gap sizes from left to right, then the number of spaces at the end of the line.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` words separated by spaces.
outputFormat: For each line print `k`, the `k - 1` gaps and the trailing spaces, separated by spaces.
constraints: Every word has between 1 and W lowercase letters.

examples.note: Line 1 is "this is an": 8 letters and 8 spaces in 2 gaps, so the gaps are 4 and 4. Line 2 is the last line, "example of text": single spaces and 1 trailing space.

hints: Fill a line greedily: add the next word if the line length with one space before it is at most `W`.
For a normal line divide the spare spaces over the gaps with `divmod`; the left gaps get the extra ones.
Treat a one-word line and the last line separately: all gaps are 1 and the rest is trailing space.

n, w = map(int, input().split())
words = input().split()

explanation: Pack words greedily, then compute the gap sizes with an integer division of the spare spaces by the number of gaps. The last line and one-word lines use single spaces.

code.python:
n, w = map(int, input().split())
words = input().split()

i = 0
out = []
while i < n:
    j = i
    length = len(words[i])
    while j + 1 < n and length + 1 + len(words[j + 1]) <= w:
        j += 1
        length += 1 + len(words[j])
    count = j - i + 1
    letters = sum(len(x) for x in words[i:j + 1])
    if j == n - 1 or count == 1:
        gaps = [1] * (count - 1)
        trailing = w - letters - (count - 1)
    else:
        spaces = w - letters
        slots = count - 1
        base, extra = divmod(spaces, slots)
        gaps = [base + 1 if k < extra else base for k in range(slots)]
        trailing = 0
    out.append(" ".join(map(str, [count] + gaps + [trailing])))
    i = j + 1
print("\n".join(out))
